_purpose: Rules that keep expert outreach from being spam. outreach.py refuses to draft anything that breaks a rule.
require_personalisation: body must cite at least one of the expert's own papers listed in experts.json
require_study_evidence: all gates passed (gates file has no FAIL)
result is new since the last email on this topic

question_mail._what: An e-mail that asks whether something is known or right may go out before the claim is settled. Its EVIDENCE.json says kind 'question' and question_gates_passed; the body must say what is unchecked.

recurring._what: Outreach is a standing activity, not a one-off. Specs wait in outbox/outreach/; the daily task 'Millennium follow-up drafts' runs outreach.run_queue and sends the next one the rules allow. Once a week an AI session looks for a new checked result worth one question to one researcher.

endorsement_requests._what: 2026-11-26 user: 'do the forward for me ... that would be automation too'. arXiv asks a first-time submitter for an endorsement and says to forward its code to someone who may endorse. endorsement.py does that as a standing step: it writes one request at a time into outbox/outreach/, and the queue sends it under every rule above. Only people arXiv itself lists as endorsers for the category, whose work the paper cites and whose address is printed in public, are on a need's list. The next person is asked after days_between_requests days of silence, at most max_people_per_need people per need, and nothing more goes out once anybody has answered until an AI session has read the answer. Why so few: an endorser vouches with their own name, and asking many people at once for one paper is what the rest of this file exists to prevent.

_auto_send_note: 2026-11-07 user: follow-ups, updates/replies AND first contacts are sent automatically. 2026-11-25 user: 'my lab own rule u can change, not only for contact but emails sent too, make it usual thing recurring ... can ask and if promote need then can try'. So the pace is now steady instead of rare: at most 2 new people in 7 days and 8 in 30 days (was 2 in 30), 60 days before the same person hears of a NEW result (was 180), and a question may be asked before every gate has passed if it says what is unchecked. Unchanged, because they are what keeps this from being spam: one recipient, 420 words, AI disclosure, 'no reply is needed', one specific question, the expert's own paper cited, a public source for the address, one unanswered e-mail per person, one follow-up at most, never again after 'declined'. The AI session may adjust these numbers when the results justify it and must write the reason here.
_ai_send_note: 2026-11-07 user: 'u do all urself'. Updates and answers to experts who are already in contact are written AND sent by the AI session (same rules: word limit, AI disclosure, no-obligation line, question). Unattended scripts never send generated answers; gmail_inbox.py queues a needs_ai job instead. First contacts go through outreach.py propose or the queue (approved 2026-11-07, recurring since 2026-11-25).
